We had our beloved dog's patellar luxation (patella) surgery performed at this hospital.

At this hospital, we were told that surgery on both legs and a one-week hospital stay would be necessary. Another hospital had told us that hospitalization would only be one day, so a week-long stay was actually reassuring. However, I honestly hesitated when I learned that surgery on both legs was necessary, as I had thought it would only be one.

However, the doctor explained in detail that there was a possibility that the right leg might also need surgery eventually, that the unoperated leg would bear more burden after the surgery, and that there wouldn't be a significant difference in surgery time between one leg and both. I was convinced and scheduled the surgery that same day.

Considering the worry I would have had about the unoperated leg, I'm truly glad we had both legs operated on.

During the one-week hospital stay, the doctor and staff treated our dog with great kindness and warmth. Our dog didn't seem to find the hospital a scary place, and even after the surgery, she came for each check-up with a smile.

Looking back now, the main reasons I decided to have the surgery here were probably the doctor's thorough explanation and the warm atmosphere of the entire hospital. I'm so glad I found a hospital that not only has excellent technical skills, but also a very welcoming and homey atmosphere where I can confidently entrust my precious family to their care.

Thank you so much for taking care of my beloved cat's treatment.

The doctors and nurses were all incredibly kind and treated animals with such gentleness. The treatment was prompt and professional, and they were very dedicated to treating my cat's FIP. Thanks to them, I felt completely at ease entrusting my cat to their care.

During her hospitalization, they provided meticulous care, sending photos and thoroughly explaining the test results and her condition, which I truly appreciated.

Upon discharge, they even drew a cute illustration of my cat by hand and wrote a detailed record of her hospitalization, which I found incredibly touching.

The hospital itself was clean and had a calming atmosphere, making it a very trustworthy hospital.

I am truly grateful that I was able to entrust my precious family member to their care with such peace of mind.

Thank you so much for treating my cat with such care.

This is a very conscientious clinic, and I felt completely at ease entrusting my pet's care to them.

I am especially grateful to Dr. Isono for his help.

In early February, my cat injured its tail, and I took it to this clinic.

A hospital near my home recommended tail amputation because it wasn't their specialty.

However, here, they not only examined the X-rays but also thoroughly checked my cat's condition, and determined that it was a subluxation and could be fixed with a bandage. Thanks to their treatment, my cat made a full recovery.

I was deeply impressed by their approach of not unilaterally deciding on a treatment plan, but instead carefully listening to my pet's personality and condition, as well as my wishes as the owner, and working together to find the best course of action.

Now, my cat has recovered so well that it can run around and play with its younger sibling cat with great energy. ☺️

Thank you so much for saving my precious family member.

I am truly grateful.

We bring our medium-sized dog to this clinic. The head veterinarian, along with the other doctors and nurses, are incredibly friendly and helpful.

They don't just provide treatment; they take the time to care for our dog with love and attention, which gives us great peace of mind when entrusting our beloved family member to their care.

Our female dog underwent laparoscopic spaying. While open surgery is more common these days, this clinic, part of a group of clinics, had large, specialized equipment, so we opted for laparoscopic surgery, even though it was a bit more expensive. She was able to go for a walk the next day, and her post-operative recovery was excellent with a very small incision. As a first-time dog owner, I remember feeling very relieved.

We will continue to bring our dog here, and we hope you will continue to provide excellent care. 🐾🐾

Dear 31 Ishi 24 Ko (31 Uchi),

Thank you very much for your kind review.

We will continue to strive to provide even better medical care and hospitality. We look forward to your continued support.

The Staff of Gotokuji Animal Medical Center

My mother apparently received treatment there.

It seems to be a generally kind animal hospital, but I was annoyed by their insistence on registering for LINE.

It's no wonder, considering they have Dr. Kaoru Yoshiike who uses LINE for consultations.

For me, it's a nuisance.

My cat received excellent care from Dr. Yamamoto. Thanks to him, he was able to extend his life despite being elderly and suffering from illness. Thank you very much.

His clear and to-the-point explanations, diagnoses, prescriptions, and advice are very trustworthy. Not only that, he is also a wonderful doctor who is able to empathize with his patients.

The staff are also very warm and kind, which makes me feel at ease.

I believe this is a doctor and a clinic where I can safely entrust my pet's life.

This is a veterinary hospital near my parents' house. I had no complaints about Dr. Yoshiike's treatment, but...

...I deducted one star because of this situation.

The issue with the animals' diet has been resolved, so please don't worry about that. I just want an accurate diagnosis and prescription.

One of my two male cats recently developed kidney failure and was receiving subcutaneous infusions at home. However, over the past few days, he began to feel lethargic after the infusions and was unable to urinate, so he was hospitalized. However, just before Golden Week, I suddenly received a phone call saying, "We're taking the day off tomorrow and will only have nurses on staff. We can't handle emergencies, so please seek care elsewhere." Using the holidays as an excuse, I was left out in the cold.

He had no appetite and still couldn't urinate, so we ended up sending him home exhausted with a catheter attached.

I was told to seek care elsewhere...Golden Week is just around the corner... They referred me to an affiliated 24-hour emergency hospital, but it was quite far away and my owner has trouble walking, so when I asked, "Can you recommend another hospital?" they just replied, "You'll have to find one yourself."

After discussing it with my family, I found a hospital nearby that makes house calls, so I decided to go there. When I called them back later, only a nurse answered the phone. Should I leave my lethargic patient and go enjoy my vacation??
In the end, the hospital I was planning to go to said, "I guess we'll have to bring him in first," so I gave up and instead arranged for them to make a house call at another hospital in Kinuta today, but they're closed from tomorrow even if he's admitted (I got the impression this vet was very responsible).

He's just getting weaker and weaker, and to be honest, I think he's in danger. But as his owner, I'm grasping at straws. I can only pray from the bottom of my heart that the doctor who will be coming today will somehow save him.

Yoshiike Veterinary Hospital...
I'm so frustrated I can't even find the words to describe it.
I've been seeing them for several years, and this is how they treat me...
I want my medical expenses refunded.
